unit

Unit

  • [[##rule 109.2|109.2.]] The State of all Game Objects in the Play Area is also Public Information. Examples: If a Unit is Buffed If a Gear is Exhausted Etc.
  • [[##rule 133.4.a.2|133.4.a.2.]] Unit and Gear are permanent types.
  • [[##rule 140|140.]] Units
  • [[##rule 141|141.]] Unit is:
  • [[##rule 141.1.a.1|141.1.a.1.]] Units are at one of several Locations while on the Board: a Battleﬁeld or their Base.
  • [[##rule 141.1.a.2|141.1.a.2.]] Units and their details are Public Information while on the Board.
  • [[##rule 141.1.a.3|141.1.a.3.]] Units can be chosen, affected, or manipulated by spells, affects, or game actions that specify Units.
  • [[##rule 141.1.a.4|141.1.a.4.]] Units can be Killed. See rule 428. Kill for more information.
  • [[##rule 141.1.b.1|141.1.b.1.]] Units are treated as Cards, similar to when in the Hand.
  • [[##rule 141.1.b.2|141.1.b.2.]] They retain the properties of being a Unit, but are not on the Board and thus cannot take actions or be affected by spells, abilities, or game actions that target Units on the Board.
  • [[##rule 141.1.b.3|141.1.b.3.]] Units can be affected by spells and game effects that target Units in the Trash.
  • [[##rule 142|142.]] Damage is a marked value that is applied to Units.
  • [[##rule 142.3|142.3.]] Damage tracks how close a Unit is to being Killed. See rule 428. Kill for more information.
  • [[##rule 143|143.]] Units have multiple Intrinsic Properties unique to them:
  • [[##rule 143.1|143.1.]] Tag: A Unit has zero or more Tags representing one or more champions, regions, factions, or species it belongs to.
  • [[##rule 143.2|143.2.]] Might: The combat statistic of a Unit. Used to determine a Unit's contribution to Combat, as well as when it is Killed by damaging effects.
  • [[##rule 143.2.a|143.2.a.]] If a Unit ever has nonzero damage marked on it equalling or exceeding its Might, it is Killed.
  • [[##rule 143.3|143.3.]] Units can have damage marked on them.
  • [[##rule 143.3.a|143.3.a.]] When spells, abilities, or other game effects deal damage, Units mark that damage on them temporarily. This can be tracked with coins, dice, or other markers, or by memory.
  • [[##rule 143.3.b|143.3.b.]] Damage is Healed from Units at two speciﬁc times:
  • [[##rule 143.4|143.4.]] Units enter the Board exhausted.
  • [[##rule 144|144.]] Units have the Inherent Ability to perform a Standard Move.
  • [[##rule 144.2|144.2.]] Exhausting the Unit is the Cost for this action.
  • [[##rule 144.3|144.3.]] Players may perform multiple Units' standard move simultaneously.
  • [[##rule 144.3.c|144.3.c.]] The Costs of Exhausting the Units are also paid Simultaneously.
  • [[##rule 144.4|144.4.]] The Destinations where Units can Move to with their Standard Move are restricted:
  • [[##rule 144.4.a|144.4.a.]] Units may move from their Base to a Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 144.4.b|144.4.b.]] Units may move from a Battleﬁeld to their Base.
  • [[##rule 144.4.c|144.4.c.]] Ganking is a unique ability that affects a Unit's Standard Move
  • [[##rule 144.4.c.1|144.4.c.1.]] Units with Ganking may use their Standard Move to Move from Battleﬁeld to Battleﬁeld. See rule 810. Ganking for more information.
  • [[##rule 145|145.]] Units may have Activated Abilities.
  • [[##rule 145.2|145.2.]] The Activated Ability of Units may be executed at any time during the controlling player's Main Phase during an Open State, and not during a Showdown.
  • [[##rule 146|146.]] Units have a Location.
  • [[##rule 162.2.b|162.2.b.]] Some Power is Universal and can be used to pay for costs of any Domain.
  • [[##rule 169.6|169.6.]] Any number of Units can be present at a Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 169.10.a|169.10.a.]] Battleﬁelds can be “occupied.” This means they have a Unit present.
  • [[##rule 187.3.a|187.3.a.]] Contested is a temporary status applied to the battleﬁeld when a Unit controlled by a Player who does not currently Control that Battleﬁeld Moves or otherwise becomes present there.
  • [[##rule 187.3.a.1|187.3.a.1.]] Units moving to or being played to a battleﬁeld apply Contested status if that battleﬁeld is not already contested and that Unit’s controller does not already control that battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 187.4|187.4.]] Control is established by having Units at a Battleﬁeld at the end of a Showdown or Combat after applying the contested status.
  • [[##rule 187.4.a|187.4.a.]] If a player controls Units at a Battleﬁeld, outside of Combat, they maintain Control of that Battleﬁeld for as long as they have Units at that Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 187.4.c|187.4.c.]] If a player has no Units at a Battleﬁeld and the turn is in an Open state, they lose Control of that Battleﬁeld in the following cleanup, unless there is a Combat or Showdown ongoing there.
  • [[##rule 316.4.a|316.4.a.]] A Combat occurs as a result of Units controlled by opposing players being present at the same Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 317.2.b|317.2.b.]] Insert “2c. Heal all Units.”
  • [[##rule 323.2|323.2.]] 2. Assign or Remove the Attacker or Defender designation from Units as needed if there is a Combat in progress
  • [[##rule 323.2.a|323.2.a.]] If there are Units present at the Battleﬁeld the Combat is taking place at, but do not have a designation, they gain the same designation as their Controller now
  • [[##rule 323.2.b|323.2.b.]] If there are Units present at the Battleﬁeld the Combat is taking place at, but have the opposite designation of their controller, they lose that designation, and gain the same designation as their controller now
  • [[##rule 323.2.c|323.2.c.]] If there are Units at locations other than the Battleﬁeld that the Combat is taking place at, but have either Attacker or Defender designations, they lose those designations now
  • [[##rule 323.4|323.4.]] 3a. All Units that have non-zero Damage marked on them equalling or exceeding their Might that have Deathknell abilities will trigger their Deathknell ability now, making note of their current location, attributes, and other information relevant to add the trigger as a Pending Item See rule 808 Deathknell for more information.
  • [[##rule 323.5|323.5.]] 3b. All Units that have non-zero Damage marked on them equalling or exceeding their Might are killed and placed in their owners' Trash.
  • [[##rule 323.6|323.6.]] 4. If the turn is in an Open State, Battleﬁelds with no Units occupying them and no Showdown or Combat ongoing become Uncontrolled.
  • [[##rule 323.7|323.7.]] 5. Recall all Unattached non-Unit Gear at Battleﬁelds, and all Permanents and Runes in Bases other than their controller’s. Remove all Hidden cards from all Battleﬁelds that are not controlled by the same player and place them in their owner's Trash.
  • [[##rule 323.9.a|323.9.a.]] The Combat remains Staged at that Battleﬁeld as long as there are Units present from two opposing players there.
  • [[##rule 355.2|355.2.]] For Units, choose a valid Location where that Unit will be placed upon being Played.
  • [[##rule 355.2.b|355.2.b.]] Some Game Effects may grant players permission to play Units to locations that are not normally Valid. Such locations become Valid for the purposes of Playing the Unit.
  • [[##rule 355.4|355.4.]] For Spells and Abilities that Move one or more Units, choose a valid Location as the Move Destination for each Move that will be performed.
  • [[##rule 355.4.a|355.4.a.]] A valid Location is one other than the Units’ current Location where they are allowed to be present.
  • [[##rule 355.14.a|355.14.a.]] If a card speciﬁes that an amount of damage may be split among some number of Units, then each Unit chosen is Targeted.
  • [[##rule 358.2|358.2.]] Ensure that the outcome of the effect of this card being played would not create an illegal state. Example: Check that a spell's execution does not create a state where a Battleﬁeld has Units controlled by 3 different players.
  • [[##rule 359.2.c|359.2.c.]] If it is a Unit, it enters the Board exhausted at the Location that was chosen.
  • [[##rule 383.4.a.1|383.4.a.1.]] These are commonly structured as “When you play me…” for Units and “When you play this…” for Gear.
  • [[##rule 383.4.c|383.4.c.]] Conquer Effects are Triggered Abilities with a Condition of a Unit participating in, and successfully Conquering a Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 383.4.c.2|383.4.c.2.]] This category of Triggered Abilities encompasses only those that are triggered from Units that were present during the Conquer action, or Abilities that the player that performed the Conquer action.
  • [[##rule 383.4.c.2.a|383.4.c.2.a.]] The Conquer Abilities of Units are put on the Chain as Pending Items after the Unit(s) these effects correspond to are present at a Battleﬁeld when a player gains control of it and gains 1 Victory Point from Conquering.
  • [[##rule 383.4.d|383.4.d.]] Hold Effects are Triggered Abilities with a Condition of a Unit being present at a Battleﬁeld during the Beginning phase when a player scores Victory Points from Holding.
  • [[##rule 383.4.d.2|383.4.d.2.]] This category of Triggered Abilities encompasses only those that are triggered from Units that were present during the Hold action, or Abilities that the player that performed the Hold action.
  • [[##rule 383.4.d.2.a|383.4.d.2.a.]] The Hold Abilities of Units are put on the Chain as Pending Items after the Unit these effects correspond to are present at a Battleﬁeld when a player maintains control of it and Gains 1 Victory Point during their Beginning Phase from Holding.
  • [[##rule 383.4.e|383.4.e.]] Attack Triggers are Triggered Abilities that trigger when a Unit gains the Attacker designation for the ﬁrst time during a combat.
  • [[##rule 383.4.e.2|383.4.e.2.]] These Triggered Abilities are put on the Chain as Pending Items after the Unit these effects correspond to gains the Attacker designation during Combat.
  • [[##rule 383.4.e.2.a|383.4.e.2.a.]] These triggers will only have their condition checked once per combat, despite a Unit being able to gain and lose the Attacker designation multiple times in the same combat.
  • [[##rule 383.4.f|383.4.f.]] Defend Triggers are Triggered Abilities that trigger when a Unit gains the Defender designation for the ﬁrst time during a combat.
  • [[##rule 383.4.f.2|383.4.f.2.]] These Triggered Abilities are put on the Chain as Pending Items after the Unit these effects correspond to gains the Defender designation during Combat.
  • [[##rule 383.4.f.2.a|383.4.f.2.a.]] These triggers will only have their condition checked once per combat, despite a Unit being able to gain and lose the Defender designation multiple times in the same combat.
  • [[##rule 392|392.]] Delayed Abilities are not associated with Units or Gear; they are created by other Abilities or Spells. As such they are executed when their condition and/or speciﬁed time occurs regardless of whether the source of the Delayed Ability is still on the board or not.
  • [[##rule 400.2|400.2.]] When an Ability with the [Add] action is ﬁnalized it resolves immediately instead of becoming a Chain Item, like a Unit or Gear.
  • [[##rule 410.1.b.3|410.1.b.3.]] As long as it does not result in any forbidden action being taken or game state being created. Example: A player can't use the Standard Move discretionary action to move a unit to a Battleﬁeld that's already occupied by Units controlled by two other players.
  • [[##rule 414.1.b|414.1.b.]] A Unit that is already Exhausted cannot be Exhausted again.
  • [[##rule 414.1.c|414.1.c.]] If a Unit is instructed to be Exhausted while it is already Exhausted, nothing additional happens.
  • [[##rule 415.1.b|415.1.b.]] A Unit that is already Ready cannot be Readied again.
  • [[##rule 415.1.c|415.1.c.]] If a Unit is instructed to be Readied while it is already Ready, nothing additional happens.
  • [[##rule 417.1.b|417.1.b.]] To Deal Damage to Units, mark the speciﬁed amount of Damage on the Unit.
  • [[##rule 417.1.d|417.1.d.]] Damage can be Dealt to more than one Unit at the same time.
  • [[##rule 417.6.c|417.6.c.]] Damage Dealt as a result of being assigned during Combat has the Units as its source.
  • [[##rule 418.1|418.1.]] Damage being cleared from Units is Healing.
  • [[##rule 418.2|418.2.]] More than one Unit can be Healed at the same time.
  • [[##rule 420.2.b|420.2.b.]] The Standard Move inherent to Units may also cause Movement. See rule 144.for more information on the Standard Move.
  • [[##rule 420.3|420.3.]] The Standard Move inherent to Units is a Discretionary Action.
  • [[##rule 420.3.a|420.3.a.]] The Cost is Exhausting one or more Units.
  • [[##rule 420.3.b|420.3.b.]] The Effect is Moving those Unit.
  • [[##rule 423.1|423.1.]] Stunning is the act of selecting one or more Units on the Board and rendering them Stunned.
  • [[##rule 423.1.a|423.1.a.]] Stunned is a binary state. A Unit is Stunned or it isn't.
  • [[##rule 426.1|426.1.]] Bufﬁng is the action of placing a Buff counter on a Unit. See rule 701. Buffs for more information.
  • [[##rule 428.5.a|428.5.a.]] The Killed Unit or Gear is said to be Killed by that Game Object.
  • [[##rule 428.5.b|428.5.b.]] A spell or ability that contains a Kill instruction is responsible for Killing the Unit or Gear.
  • [[##rule 428.5.c|428.5.c.]] When one or more Units is killed due to a Cleanup, that kill action is attributed to the spell or ability that resolved immediately prior to that Cleanup that dealt damage to the Unit or Units. The player responsible for the deal action is responsible for the kill action.
  • [[##rule 437.2|437.2.]] When damage is Prevented, it is replaced with an event where it deals that much damage reduced by the Prevent Value tracked on the Unit speciﬁcally.
  • [[##rule 437.3|437.3.]] When damage is dealt this way, reduce the Prevent Value being tracked on the Unit affected by the Prevent action by the prevented amount.
  • [[##rule 437.3.a|437.3.a.]] If the Prevent Value is 0 or less, then Prevent is no longer being tracked on the Unit in question, and the effect expires.
  • [[##rule 437.4|437.4.]] Damage dealt to a Unit that has that all of that damage Prevented is not considered to have been dealt to it at all.
  • [[##rule 437.5|437.5.]] Damage can still be assigned to Units in combat that are affected by Prevent. The damage dealt as a result of that assignment will be affected by the Prevent action.
  • [[##rule 437.5.a|437.5.a.]] Damage can be assigned to a Unit up to a value that would be Lethal considering the Prevent Value of all Prevent Actions on a Unit. Example: A unit with 2 [M] is being assigned damage in the combat damage step. The unit has “prevent the ﬁrst 3 damage I would take each combat.” The unit would need to be assigned 5 damage in order to have lethal damage assigned to it.
  • [[##rule 442.2.a|442.2.a.]] In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battleﬁelds with Staged Combats or Combats in Progress are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units controlled by Players not involved in those Combats or who don't already have permanents at that Battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 442.2.b|442.2.b.]] In Modes of Play with teammates, Battleﬁelds Controlled by a player’s teammates are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units that player controls.
  • [[##rule 442.2.c|442.2.c.]] If an action would require a Move that would cause a Unit to become present in a Location where it cannot move for any reason, such as a Battleﬁeld with two players that are not the controller of the Unit performing this Move action are in a Combat or such a Combat is Staged, it instead Recalls. See rule 449. Recalls for more information.
  • [[##rule 442.3|442.3.]] Units are the only Permanents that can Move.
  • [[##rule 443|443.]] Players may choose to move their Units with the Standard Move. See rule 144.for more information on the Standard Move.
  • [[##rule 445|445.]] The Destination becomes Contested if it is a Battleﬁeld not controlled by the controller of the Unit or Units that moved.
  • [[##rule 446|446.]] Units may cause a Showdown without a Combat when they Move.
  • [[##rule 446.1|446.1.]] A Showdown is opened when a Move causes a Battleﬁeld to become Contested while it has no Units present from any player other than those that just moved.
  • [[##rule 447|447.]] Units may cause Combat when they Move.
  • [[##rule 447.1|447.1.]] A Combat is opened when a Move causes a Battleﬁeld to become Contested and Units controlled by opposing players, or when a Move causes Units controlled by opposing players to become present in the same Battleﬁeld where a Showdown is ongoing. See rule 454. Combat for more information.
  • [[##rule 456.1|456.1.]] If more than one Battleﬁeld has Units controlled by opposing players at it at the same time, the Turn Player decides which Combat to resolve ﬁrst.
  • [[##rule 457|457.]] Combat can only occur between Units controlled by exactly two players.
  • [[##rule 457.1|457.1.]] In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battleﬁelds with Staged Combats or Combats in Progress are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units controlled by Players not involved in those Combats or who don't already have Units at that Battleﬁeld. See rule 442.2.a.for more information on Invalid Destinations.
  • [[##rule 457.2|457.2.]] In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battleﬁelds with Staged Combats or Combats in Progress are Invalid to be chosen as a location to play one or more Units by a player not involved in that Combat by any means,
  • [[##rule 457.2.a|457.2.a.]] If an effect would require a Unit be played to a Battleﬁeld with a Staged Combat or a Combat in Progress, where the controller of the played unit is not a participant, instead the Unit is played to its controller's Base.
  • [[##rule 457.2.b|457.2.b.]] Any subsequent to "here" in the corresponding effect is reassigned to the Controller's Base, where the Unit was played. Any further effects that may be invalidated are invalidated as if the effect was mistargeted. See rule 355.6. Targeting for more information on Mistargeting.
  • [[##rule 459.2.b.3.a|459.2.b.3.a.]] If a Unit controlled by the Attacker becomes present at this Battleﬁeld after this moment, it will gain the Attacker designation during the Cleanup phase following the action that caused it to become present
  • [[##rule 459.2.b.4.a|459.2.b.4.a.]] If a Unit controlled by the Defender becomes present at this Battleﬁeld after this moment it will gain the Defender designation during the Cleanup phase following the action that caused it to become present
  • [[##rule 460.2.c|460.2.c.]] Starting with the Attacker, each player assigns an amount of damage equal to their summed Might among the other's Units.
  • [[##rule 460.2.c.3|460.2.c.3.]] Units must have lethal damage assigned to them in full before damage is assigned to a different Unit. Example: If a player has 5 damage to distribute among four 3 Might units, they may not choose to assign 2 damage to one of the units and 1 damage to each of the remaining 3. They must assign at least 3 damage to one, and the remaining 2 to another.
  • [[##rule 460.2.c.4|460.2.c.4.]] Units cannot have more damage assigned to them than the minimum required to constitute lethal damage unless no further units remain to have damage assigned to them.
  • [[##rule 460.2.c.6|460.2.c.6.]] If multiple Units have abilities or effects that require a player to assign them damage with the same priority, that player may assign damage to those units in any order. Example: A player is assigning damage to the following units: two units with Tank ("I must be assigned combat damage ﬁrst.") and one unit with no abilities. That player chooses one of the units with Tank and assigns combat damage to it. Then they must assign any remaining damage ﬁrst to the other unit with Tank, then to the unit with no abilities.
  • [[##rule 460.2.c.7|460.2.c.7.]] If a Unit has one or more Abilities or effects applying to it that demand it be assigned damage in a speciﬁc way that is exclusionary, then the assigning player chooses only one of those abilities to apply when assigning damage. Example: Caitlyn, Patrolling ("I must be assigned combat damage last.") has been given the Tank ability ("I must be assigned combat damage ﬁrst."). A player is assigning damage to this Caitlyn with Tank and two units with no abilities. That player can’t fulﬁll both of Caitlyn’s damage requirements, so they may choose to assign damage to Caitlyn ﬁrst, fulﬁlling the Tank requirement, or last, fulﬁlling Caitlyn’s printed requirement. They can’t choose to apply damage to Caitlyn in between the other two units, because that wouldn’t fulﬁll either requirement.
  • [[##rule 461.1.a.1|461.1.a.1.]] Insert “3c. Heal all Units.”
  • [[##rule 461.3.c|461.3.c.]] Units at this battleﬁeld inherit the same combat result as their controllers
  • [[##rule 461.3.d|461.3.d.]] There is “No Result” if either both Players have units present during this step, or neither player has units present during this step.
  • [[##rule 461.3.d.1|461.3.d.1.]] If “No Result” was reached, and both players have units remaining, stage a Combat at this battleﬁeld.
  • [[##rule 461.5|461.5.]] 1. If no Showdown or Combat is staged at this location, the player with Units remaining here Establishes Control.
  • [[##rule 461.5.b|461.5.b.]] If there are no Units remaining here controlled by any player, the Battleﬁeld becomes Uncontrolled.
  • [[##rule 461.7.a|461.7.a.]] Remove Attacker and Defender Designation from all Units and Players.
  • [[##rule 484.8.c.2|484.8.c.2.]] Players may not issue Standard Movement to their Teammate's Units.
  • [[##rule 484.8.d|484.8.d.]] Friendly describes controlled Game Objects by a player or their Teammate. Example: "When I am played, ready a friendly unit" could target a player's own Units or their teammate's Units.
  • [[##rule 702|702.]] Buffs are objects placed on Units.
  • [[##rule 702.2.a|702.2.a.]] To Buff a Unit, a player chooses a Unit and then places a buff on it. That Unit is Buffed for as long as the buff remains on it.
  • [[##rule 702.2.b|702.2.b.]] Spending a Buff removes a single Buff counter from a Unit.
  • [[##rule 702.2.b.1|702.2.b.1.]] A buff cannot be spent from a Unit that does not have a buff.
  • [[##rule 702.3|702.3.]] There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time.
  • [[##rule 702.3.a|702.3.a.]] If a Buff is added, or instructed to be added, on a Unit that already has a Buff, it is not placed instead.
  • [[##rule 703|703.]] Each Buff individually contributes +1 Might to a Unit.
  • [[##rule 705|705.]] If a Unit leaves play, remove all Buffs from it.
  • [[##rule 708|708.]] A Unit "is Mighty" as long as its Might is 5 or greater.
  • [[##rule 709|709.]] A Unit "becomes Mighty" at the moment its Might changes from being less than 5 to being 5 or greater. Example: A Unit with Might 4 that gets +1 [M] becomes Mighty. Example: A Unit with Might 5 that gets +1 [M] does not become Mighty, because it was already Mighty.
  • [[##rule 741|741.]] Some card text refers to Units in particular ways:
  • [[##rule 805.1|805.1.]] Accelerate is a Unit ability.
  • [[##rule 806.3|806.3.]] Action does not alter the function of any instruction of the corresponding card or effect it is on. It is only permission. Example: Playing a Unit with Action still has the inherent restrictions of playing Units without Action. It can only be played to the controlling player's base or a battleﬁeld they control.
  • [[##rule 813.3.a|813.3.a.]] Playing Units with Reaction still has the inherent restrictions of playing Units without Reaction. It can only be played to the controlling player's base or a battleﬁeld they control.
  • [[##rule 818.1.b|818.1.b.]] Equip has a cost to activate and Attaches the card with Equip to a chosen Unit when the cost is paid.
  • [[##rule 818.1.b.2|818.1.b.2.]] The chosen Unit will become the Top-Most Card for the Attach action.
  • [[##rule 818.2|818.2.]] When the Attach action completes from this keyword, the Unit that was chosen is considered to have been Equipped by the Gear with this ability.
  • [[##rule 819.1.d|819.1.d.]] Quick-Draw is functionally short for “[Reaction]” and “When you play this, attach it to a Unit you control.” See rule 716. Attachment for more information.
  • [[##rule 821.1.a|821.1.a.]] Weaponmaster is present on Units.
  • [[##rule 821.3|821.3.]] Weaponmaster, and whether or not a unit has Weaponmaster, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or d by other Game Effects.
  • [[##rule 822.1.a|822.1.a.]] It is present on Units.
  • [[##rule 822.1.b|822.1.b.]] It is functionally short for "I may be played to a battleﬁeld where you control Units" and “I have [Reaction] as long as I’m being played to a battleﬁeld where you control Units.”
  • [[##rule 822.1.c|822.1.c.]] It is a passive ability that adds options to locations that are valid for a Unit to be played to during the Make Relevant Choices step of Playing a Card See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information
  • [[##rule 822.3.a|822.3.a.]] Other effects and permissions may still enable this Unit to be able to be played to the selected location, but Ambush’s permission will not be valid
  • [[##rule 823.1.a|823.1.a.]] Hunt is present on Units.
  • [[##rule 825|825.]] Unique
  • [[##rule 825.1|825.1.]] Unique is a Deck Constraint Permission.
  • [[##rule 825.2|825.2.]] Unique is not functionally short for any rules text, and instead provides a restriction to players during Deck Construction.
  • [[##rule 825.2.a|825.2.a.]] A Deck can contain only one card of a given name if the card has Unique
  • [[##rule 825.2.b|825.2.b.]] If a card is a Signature card and is also Unique, then that Deck can contain any combination of three Signature cards, but still only one of each named Unique card.
  • [[##rule 825.3|825.3.]] Cards with Unique have no additional effects during gameplay.
  • [[##rule 825.4|825.4.]] Unique, and whether or not a Card has Unique, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or d by other Game Effects.

units cannot move

Units Cannot Move

  • [[##rule 144.4.a.1|144.4.a.1.]] Units cannot Move to a Battleﬁeld that already has units from 2 other players present, or where a Combat is ongoing that has 2 other players as participants.
  • [[##rule 444.2|444.2.]] Units cannot Move to a Battleﬁeld that already has units from 2 other players present by any means.

units, gear

Units, Gear

  • [[##rule 337.1.c|337.1.c.]] Units, Gear, and abilities that Add resources resolve immediately when Finalized and do not progress to Step 2: Execute. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

unit’s location

Unit’s Location

  • [[##rule 146.1|146.1.]] A Unit’s Location is the Base or Battleﬁeld it currently occupies.

unordered

Unordered

  • [[##rule 108.2.c|108.2.c.]] Cards in each player’s Trash are unordered. Their sequence does not matter, and they may be reorganized.
  • [[##rule 108.6.d|108.6.d.]] The cards in the banishment are unordered. Their sequence does not matter, and they may be reorganized.

group V

valid

Valid

  • [[##rule 355.2.a|355.2.a.]] By default, Valid locations include the controller’s Base or a Battleﬁeld the controller controls.
  • [[##rule 355.2.b|355.2.b.]] Some Game Effects may grant players permission to play Units to locations that are not normally Valid. Such locations become Valid for the purposes of Playing the Unit.

valid damage

Valid Damage

  • [[##rule 417.1.e|417.1.e.]] Valid Damage is a positive integer amount, greater than or equal to 1 Damage.
  • [[##rule 417.1.e.1|417.1.e.1.]] Only Valid Damage is Dealt. Example: A unit has “when I take damage, give me +2 [M] this turn.” A spell is played that Prevents the next 3 damage the unit would take. If a player plays Hextech Ray targeting the unit, it will take no damage and its triggered ability will not trigger. If that player had played Void Seeker instead, it would be Dealt 1 and trigger its ability. Example: A unit is present at Void Gate. A spell is played that Prevents the next 3 damage the unit would take. If a player plays Hextech Ray targeting the unit, it will take no damage - in order to apply the Bonus Damage from Void Gate, the Deal game action would have to occur, and Hextech Ray did not Deal any damage.

victory points

Victory Points

  • [[##rule 383.4.d|383.4.d.]] Hold Effects are Triggered Abilities with a Condition of a Unit being present at a Battleﬁeld during the Beginning phase when a player scores Victory Points from Holding.

victory score

Victory Score

  • [[##rule 323.1|323.1.]] 1. If a player has points greater than or equal to the Victory Score, and more points than any opponent, that player wins.
  • [[##rule 466.1.b|466.1.b.]] When a player tries to Gain a Point through a Score, and their current Point Total is 1 point from the Victory Score of the Mode of Play or higher, the following occurs:
  • [[##rule 467|467.]] When a cleanup occurs and a player has accrued Points greater than or equal to the Victory Score for their Mode of Play, and if they have more points than any opponent, they Win the Game.
  • [[##rule 478.3|478.3.]] Victory Score: The point total a player or team must reach to win.
  • [[##rule 478.3.a|478.3.a.]] Victory Scores can be any positive number.
  • [[##rule 480.3|480.3.]] Victory Score: 8
  • [[##rule 480.6|480.6.]] Format: Best of 1. The ﬁrst player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
  • [[##rule 481.3|481.3.]] Victory Score: 8
  • [[##rule 481.6|481.6.]] Format: Best of 3. The ﬁrst player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the game. The winner of that game earns One Game Win. Players then reset the game state, remove the Battleﬁelds in play from the game, choose new Battleﬁelds from those set aside, and play again. The ﬁrst player to earn Two Game Wins wins the match.
  • [[##rule 482.3|482.3.]] Victory Score: 8
  • [[##rule 482.6|482.6.]] Format: Best of 1. The ﬁrst player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
  • [[##rule 483.3|483.3.]] Victory Score: 8
  • [[##rule 483.6|483.6.]] Format: Best of 1. The ﬁrst player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
  • [[##rule 484.3|484.3.]] Victory Score: 11
  • [[##rule 484.6|484.6.]] Format: Best of 1. The ﬁrst team to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.

vision

Vision

  • [[##rule 472.2.b|472.2.b.]] Effects for this layer can be identiﬁed by the phrase "become(s)," "give," "lose(s)," "have," "has," "is," or "are" in the text. Example: A permanent has the ability "Other friendly units have [Vision]." Other friendly units gain the Vision keyword in this layer.
  • [[##rule 817|817.]] Vision

group W

weaponmaster

Weaponmaster

  • [[##rule 725.3|725.3.]] If an Attached card has an Equip ability, the Weaponmaster keyword can that Equip ability and any abilities that passively modify that Equip ability.
  • [[##rule 821|821.]] Weaponmaster
  • [[##rule 821.1|821.1.]] Weaponmaster is a Triggered Ability keyword.
  • [[##rule 821.1.a|821.1.a.]] Weaponmaster is present on Units.
  • [[##rule 821.1.b|821.1.b.]] Weaponmaster is a Play Effect that chooses an Equipment you control and allows you to pay its Equip cost at a discount, regardless of the usual timing of the Equip ability, to Attach that Equipment to the unit with Weaponmaster.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c|821.1.c.]] Weaponmaster is functionally short for: “When you play me, you may choose a Card you control with the Equipment tag. Necessary portions of its Rules Text are no longer Inactive if they are currently Inactive. Pay the cost of its Equip ability, reduced by [A], to attach it to this unit.” See rule 716. Attachment for more information.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c.1|821.1.c.1.]] Weaponmaster can choose an Equipment whether it has an Equip ability or not.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c.2|821.1.c.2.]] The cost of the Equip ability is determined as though that Equip ability was being activated choosing the unit with the Weaponmaster ability, as modulated by any abilities that alter Equip costs.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c.5|821.1.c.5.]] If the chosen card’s Equip cost can’t be paid, if it can’t be detached from its current Top-Most card, or if it can’t be attached to the unit with the Weaponmaster ability, it stays in its current location, Attached to anything it was already Attached to.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c.6|821.1.c.6.]] The Equip ability is not activated this way, and the unit with the Weaponmaster ability is not chosen.
  • [[##rule 821.1.c.7|821.1.c.7.]] Multiple instances of Weaponmaster trigger separately, and can choose different targets.
  • [[##rule 821.1.d|821.1.d.]] If you choose the same target with multiple instances of Weaponmaster, each will resolve separately.
  • [[##rule 821.2|821.2.]] Weaponmaster has no function while on the board.
  • [[##rule 821.3|821.3.]] Weaponmaster, and whether or not a unit has Weaponmaster, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or d by other Game Effects.

while

While

  • [[##rule 364.3.a|364.3.a.]] Conditional Passive Abilities can be recognized by the occurrence of "if" or "while" as part of the statement of the ability. Example: "While I'm attacking or defending alone, I have +2 [M]." Example: "If an opponent controls a battleﬁeld, I enter ready."
  • [[##rule 383.1|383.1.]] Triggered Abilities can usually be recognized by the word "when" followed by a game action or event; the word "at" followed by a point in time during the turn sequence; or the phrase “the [Nth] time” followed by a game action or event. Examples: "When you conquer here, you may spend a buff to draw 1." "At the end of your turn, ready 2 runes." “The ﬁrst time I move each turn, you may ready something else that's exhausted.”
  • [[##rule 383.2.a|383.2.a.]] The Condition follows the When.

win the game

Win The Game

  • [[##rule 467|467.]] When a cleanup occurs and a player has accrued Points greater than or equal to the Victory Score for their Mode of Play, and if they have more points than any opponent, they Win the Game.

window of opportunity

Window Of Opportunity

  • [[##rule 316.5.c|316.5.c.]] A Showdown is a structured Window of Opportunity where Players may play cards and activate abilities with Action or Reaction. See rule 341. Showdowns for more information.
  • [[##rule 342|342.]] A Showdown is a Window of Opportunity in which Players have an Open State in which they may play Spells in an alternating fashion.

windows of opportunity

Windows Of Opportunity

  • [[##rule 326|326.]] Players can act during the following Windows of Opportunity that occur during the course of regular play:

winning point

Winning Point

  • [[##rule 466.1.a|466.1.a.]] The Winning Point has additional restrictions.
  • [[##rule 466.1.b.1|466.1.b.1.]] If the player has Scored through Hold, that player Gains the Winning Point.
  • [[##rule 466.1.b.2|466.1.b.2.]] If the player has Scored through a Conquer and has Scored every Battleﬁeld through either method this turn, that player Gains the Winning Point. If the player has Scored through a Conquer and has not Scored every Battleﬁeld this turn, that player draws a card.

wins

Wins

  • [[##rule 484.6.a.3|484.6.a.3.]] If one player Wins, then the entire team wins.
  • [[##rule 651.1|651.1.]] If only one other player is remaining after a player has conceded, the player remaining Wins.

group X

xp

Xp

  • [[##rule 728|728.]] XP
  • [[##rule 729|729.]] XP is a resource that is accrued, spent, or otherwise modiﬁed by Players through the course of play.
  • [[##rule 729.1|729.1.]] The amount of XP that a player has should be marked clearly.
  • [[##rule 729.1.a|729.1.a.]] XP is a value that can be tracked by counters, dice, cards, or any method that clearly displays the speciﬁc value of XP that is currently on a Player.
  • [[##rule 729.2|729.2.]] The amount of XP a Player has is Public Information.
  • [[##rule 730|730.]] XP can be Gained and Spent.
  • [[##rule 730.1|730.1.]] To Gain XP, increase the value of XP marked on the Player gaining it.
  • [[##rule 730.2|730.2.]] To Spend XP, reduce the value of XP marked on the Player spending it.
  • [[##rule 731|731.]] XP is not a Game Object.
  • [[##rule 731.1|731.1.]] XP cannot be targeted, readied, or exhausted.
  • [[##rule 732|732.]] XP is not shared between Allies in Game Modes with Teammates.
  • [[##rule 733|733.]] There is no limit to an amount of XP a player can accrue.
  • [[##rule 823.1.c.1|823.1.c.1.]] Hunt is functionally short for: “When I Conquer or Hold, my controller gains X XP.” See rule 728. XP for more information

group Z

zones

Zones

  • [[##rule 106|106.]] The Play Area is a collection of logical Zones that are deﬁned by their behaviors and relationships to Players. These Zones are grouped into The Board and Non-Board Zones.
  • [[##rule 128.1|128.1.]] A card will always exist in one of the many Zones described during Setup.
  • [[##rule 359.3.e.2|359.3.e.2.]] A target is illegal as the spell resolves if it no longer meets the targeting requirements of the spell, or if it has changed Zones to or from a Non-Board Zone.
  • [[##rule 359.3.e.4|359.3.e.4.]] If a target changes Zones to or from a Non-Board Zone and then returns to its original zone, it is no longer a legal target, because it's not treated as the same object. Examples: An enemy unit at a battleﬁeld is no longer a legal target if it is no longer an enemy, no longer a unit, or no longer at a battleﬁeld. A unit with 3 or less Might is no longer a legal target if it is no longer a unit or if its Might is greater than 3. Something that's exhausted is no longer a legal target if it is no longer exhausted. (It can't stop being "something.") A spell that's played from hidden can normally only target its own battleﬁeld or something at that battleﬁeld. A target for such a spell may cease to be a legal target if it moves from the battleﬁeld where that spell was played, even if the spell has no location targeting requirement otherwise.
